Revised with assistance from OpenAI Codex/GPT-6.

::: {.callout-important title="The association is descriptive and exploratory"}
The within-understood sign–speech association $\psi$ — and therefore the data-identified total expressive vocabulary $p_{\text{any}}$ — is identified from the four sources that record, per word, whether a child signs it (gestures it, in the Spanish source), says it, or both: `uk_02`, `uk_07`, `es_01` and `nz_01` (@sec-speech-sign-association). It is **descriptive / exploratory**, not a test of a hypothesis, and no causal reading is licensed: $\psi > 1$ says that a word a child understands is more often both signed and spoken than independence predicts, not that signing causes, accelerates or delays speech.

**The sources disagree, and the model says so.** $\psi$ carries a study-level term; the per-study values are the primary read, and the population value is a shrunk centre, not a consensus. The Spanish source sits close to independence where the UK and New Zealand sources do not, and why is not established. Three candidates of unknown size stand. The first is what parents counted: the Spanish column is defined to include spontaneous symbolic gestures alongside taught signs, while the other sources' "signs" columns carry no recorded definition, so the distinction cannot be drawn on either side. The second is the coverage of the Spanish gesture column, which its authors restricted to ten of the form's 21 word categories after a validity check; if the totals supplied to us carry that elimination, a word signed and said in an eliminated category is recorded as spoken only, which pushes the cross-tabulation toward independence. The third is how the children were taught, which no source records. The spread should therefore not be read as evidence about teaching or compensation. An age-varying association was investigated and rejected ; the analysis did not find an added age effect after accounting for study, but with four informing sources the spread itself is weakly identified and the prior does real work.

**Signing coverage thins with age.** Signed observations are dense from about 12 to 60 months and sparse beyond: two small sources above 72 months and one above 84, so older-age estimates depend more on the assumed smooth trajectory. Both $r(a)$ and $p_{\text{any}}$ are reported only within the comprehension-conditioned age cap. The peak age of $r(a)$ is estimated, but under a fixed three-anchor shape whose outer reference ages are asserted rather than fitted, and the signed GP's length-scale is not identified, so the signed trajectory remains substantially parametric in practice. The registered signing models describe children with Down syndrome; there is no registered TD signing model.

**Recovery checks limit how confidently the association can be reported.** The early checks found downward error in some population and study-specific association estimates. Later reporting-quality checks reduced that concern and showed why unconverged recovery fits must not be scored. These few replicates do not establish the direction or size of bias for every source. Read the per-study intervals, the prior-sensitivity results and the converged recovery evidence together. Neither crossing the independence reference nor a positive point estimate establishes a causal effect. See the [reporting-quality recovery record](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/blob/main/notes/202609031825-recovery-vg15-vg12-vg11.md).

:::
